name: Kupa
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kupa language' and 'Nupoid languages' (cite Ethnologue 25, Blench 2013, Blench 2019 Atlas 4th ed.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; 'Most Nupoid languages have 3 level tones' (citing Blench 2013). No further Kupa sources named.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2013. The Nupoid languages of West-Central Nigeria: Overview and Comparative Wordlist. Ms. (working document), 141 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: no occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'prominence' anywhere. On Kupa (p. 3, p. 5): 'Kupa is spoken in a number of villages south of the Niger near Egã, and is most closely related to Kakanda. Koelle (1854) is the only source on this language.' Section 2.3 Tone (p. 8, p. 10): 'All Nupoid languages presently studied have at least five surface tones, three level tones and two glides.. these can all be analysed as three underlying level tones' - a family-level statement, not Kupa-specific; Kupa forms in the comparative wordlist carry tone marks.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. (draft), entry 265 'Kupa', p. 54 (p. 68).
sources.note: Nothing; index-style entry only: 'Kwara State, Kogi LGA, around Abugi (52 villages).. Benue-Congo: Nupoid: Nupe group. Source(s) Blench (1987)'. No references to any Kupa description.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kupa1238 (5 references: Temilola 1987; Blench 2013; Weise 2013; Forde 1955; Koelle 1854).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliography only. Confirms Temilola 1987 is the only phonology-type reference.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana. London: Church Missionary House. (Kupa = language VI.2 in Koelle's groups.)
sources.note: Wordlist only; no statement about Kupa stress. The preface lists among the marks used '´ the common sign for the accent, e.g., á' (Koelle marked what he heard as stress across all languages; scanned text drops the diacritics, so the page scan of the 60 MB scan would be needed to read the accents on the Kupa column).
